mainTopic: Cleaning pots used for קדשים: רבי טרפון's reason, the timing and method of מריקה ושטיפה, and mixtures of stricter and less strict sacrificial meat
overview: The משנה ends by saying that a spit and a grill used for קדשים are purged in hot water. The גמרא asks why רבי טרפון lets a pot be used for the whole רגל without מריקה ושטיפה. Its first answer, that the פסוק makes the whole רגל 'one morning,' is rejected because of פיגול and נותר and because of a ברייתא of רבי נתן. Instead, the גמרא explains that each day's cooking purges the day before. It then explains the חכמים: wait until the eating time ends, then scour and rinse, as learned from two פסוקים side by side. A ברייתא brings an argument between רבי and the חכמים about whether scouring uses hot or cold water, and each side defends its reading of 'ומרק ושטף'. A new משנה deals with stricter and less strict meat cooked together. The גמרא rereads it as two cases, with taste and without taste. אביי and רבא then explain why the pot needs no scouring in the case without taste, and the גמרא shows why both cases in the משנה are needed. Finally, a ברייתא starts to derive from 'בבשרה' that only the part that absorbed is affected, and this continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Spit and grill are cleaned with hot water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes by ruling that a spit and a metal grill used for קדשים are purged in hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The spit and the grill are purged in hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It tells us how to clean a spit and a grill that were used for sacrificial meat: they are purged in hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה spoke about pots, which need מריקה ושטיפה, scouring and rinsing. A spit and a grill are a different kind of tool, so the משנה gives them their own cleaning method, הגעלה in hot water.

keyTerms.meaning: A spit, the rod used to roast meat over a fire
One purges them (does הגעלה), cleaning out absorbed taste with hot water

phrases.english: The spit and the grill
one purges them in hot water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing line of the משנה, which began on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A spit and a grill used for קדשים are cleaned by הגעלה in hot water.

steps.title: What is רבי טרפון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of רבי טרפון's rule in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי טרפון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why רבי טרפון rules as he does. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי טרפון said that if a pot was used for a חטאת at the start of the רגל, one may keep cooking in it for the whole רגל without מריקה ושטיפה each time. The גמרא wants to know what source allows treating the whole רגל as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Tarfon?
phrases.notes: He's asking about רבי טרפון's rule in the משנה: a pot used for a חטאת at the start of the רגל doesn't need scouring and rinsing again during that רגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to analyzing רבי טרפון's opinion in it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural or logical basis for treating the whole רגל as one time unit for מריקה ושטיפה

steps.title: The פסוק makes the whole רגל one morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק about the קרבן פסח: 'and you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.' This shows the תורה treats all the days of the רגל as one morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.' The תורה made all of them into one morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי טרפון's source: a פסוק that speaks of going home 'in the morning,' read as treating the whole רגל as a single morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People did not actually go home on the first morning of the רגל; they stayed in ירושלים. So 'the morning' must mean the end of the whole stay, as if all the days were one long morning. If the whole רגל counts as one time unit, one cleaning at the start covers all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall turn in the morning
One morning, one single time unit

phrases.english: As the verse states:
“And you shall turn in the morning, and go to your tents”
phrases.notes: דברים 16:7

phrases.english: the verse has made all of them
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the days of the רגל.

phrases.english: one morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא וּפָנִיתָ בַבֹּקֶר וְהָלַכְתָּ לְאֹהָלֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ופנית בבקר' treats all the days of the רגל as one morning, so one cleaning covers the whole רגל.

steps.title: Then would there be no פיגול or נותר on a רגל?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי objects: if the whole רגל is one day, then the laws of פיגול and נותר, which depend on short time limits for eating, would not apply during a רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי objects: Is there no פיגול on a רגל, and no נותר on a רגל?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחדבוי בר אמי attacks the answer of step 3. If the Torah made the whole רגל one day, that would wipe out time-based prohibitions during the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול and נותר both assume each קרבן has a fixed, short time for eating, much shorter than a whole רגל. If the whole רגל is one 'morning,' that time limit would stretch over the entire רגל, which is clearly not true. So the reading of the פסוק seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, raising a strong challenge
A קרבן made invalid by intending to eat it after its allowed time
Sacrificial meat left over past its allowed time, forbidden to eat

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami objects to this:
But is there no piggul during a Festival,
and is there no notar during a Festival?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the פסוק makes the whole רגל one morning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole רגל were one time unit, the time-based laws of פיגול and נותר would not apply during the רגל, which cannot be right.

steps.title: רבי נתן: רבי טרפון meant only this law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the possible reply 'yes, there is no פיגול or נותר on a רגל' by citing a ברייתא in which רבי נתן says רבי טרפון applied his rule only to this one law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: yes, that is so — but it is taught: רבי נתן says, רבי טרפון said this only about this law alone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone defending the answer by saying 'true, those laws don't apply on a רגל.' It then shuts that down with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן reports that רבי טרפון's 'one unit' idea applied only to מריקה ושטיפה, not to other laws like פיגול and נותר. But the פסוק, if it were his source, would make the whole רגל one day for everything. So the פסוק cannot be רבי טרפון's real source, and step 6 gives a new reason.

keyTerms.meaning: This alone, only this one law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי נתן is disagreeing with רבי טרפון. He is describing how far רבי טרפון's rule reaches, and that limit is what shows the פסוק can't be the source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out the answer of step 3, so the גמרא will need to find a different reason for רבי טרפון.

phrases.english: And if you would say: Indeed, so it is;
phrases.notes: He means: indeed, there is no פיגול or נותר during a רגל.

phrases.english: but it is taught: Rabbi Natan says:
Rabbi Tarfon did not say it
except about this alone!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the law of scouring and rinsing the pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the objection of step 4 by blocking the escape route that פיגול and נותר really don't apply on a רגל
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that the whole רגל truly is one day for every law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן says רבי טרפון limited his rule to מריקה ושטיפה alone, which a broad reading of the פסוק cannot explain, so the פסוק is not his source.

steps.title: Each day's cooking purges the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'whole רגל is one morning' reason. Instead, רבי טרפון's rule works because each day's cooking purges what the pot absorbed the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: each day's cooking acts as a purging for the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the earlier source for רבי טרפון and gives a new reason for his rule that avoids the problem about פיגול and נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason treated the whole רגל as one day, and that would have cancelled the time limits of פיגול and נותר. The new reason leaves the time limits in place. The pot never holds leftover taste for long, because each new day's cooking purges the old taste out of it. So one may keep cooking all through the רגל and scour and rinse only at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It shows the earlier explanation is being dropped.
Purging: getting absorbed taste out of a pot
For the other one, meaning the day before

steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון is not saying the leftover taste is allowed. He is saying the next day's cooking keeps purging it out, so the pot never holds forbidden נותר taste.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason fits the ברייתא of רבי נתן: רבי טרפון's rule covers only the pots, and the usual laws of פיגול and נותר stay fully in force during a רגל.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּדְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ –
phrases.english: Rather, it is like what Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: for Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Each and every day
becomes a purging for the other.
phrases.notes: Each new day's cooking pushes out the taste the pot soaked up the day before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source from step 3, after steps 4 and 5 showed it cannot stand.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that replaces the old one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון's rule comes from treating the whole רגל as one morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון's rule works because each day's cooking purges the day before, so the time limits for eating stay in place.

steps.title: What do the חכמים mean in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים's words in the משנה and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And the חכמים say: until the time of eating, and so on.' What are they saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion in the משנה, the חכמים, and asks what their short wording means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until the time of eating, scouring and rinsing' are unclear. They could mean the scouring must be done before the time runs out, or only after it ends. The גמרא wants the exact timing.

keyTerms.meaning: The time during which the קרבן may be eaten
What is he saying? A request to explain unclear wording
And so on: the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד זְמַן אֲכִילָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: until the time of eating, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The words left out are 'scouring and rinsing.'

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי טרפון's opinion to the חכמים's opinion in the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the חכמים's words 'until the time of eating' mean for when the pot must be scoured and rinsed.

steps.title: Wait until eating time ends, then scour and rinse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה explains: you wait until the eating time is over, and then you scour and rinse the pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: one waits with the pot until the time of eating is over, and then scours and rinses it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining what the חכמים meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until the time of eating' means you may wait until the eating time ends. Once it ends, you must scour and rinse the pot right then. So the חכמים do not let you keep cooking the whole רגל the way רבי טרפון does.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
One waits with it until the time of eating,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the pot. 'Until the time of eating' means until that time is over.

phrases.english: and then performs scouring and rinsing on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: מַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד זְמַן אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wait until the eating time is over, then scour and rinse the pot.

steps.title: Where does this timing come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule to wait until the eating time ends and then scour and rinse.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for the timing it just explained. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now has a clear rule, but it wants to know which פסוק shows that the scouring comes after the eating time ends.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that scouring and rinsing happen after the eating time ends.

steps.title: Two פסוקים side by side show the timing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of אבא יוסי בן אבא points to two פסוקים: 'it shall be scoured and rinsed' and 'every male among the כהנים may eat it.' Together they show you wait for the eating time, then scour and rinse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of אבא יוסי בן אבא: It is written 'and it shall be scoured and rinsed,' and it is written 'every male among the כהנים shall eat it.' How do these fit together? One waits until the eating time is over, and then scours and rinses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the source question by placing two nearby פסוקים side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says to scour and rinse the pot. The next פסוק says the כהנים may eat the קרבן. The pot is still being used while the כהנים are eating. Putting them together teaches that the scouring comes once the eating time is over.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be scoured and rinsed (ויקרא 6:21)
Every male among the כהנים shall eat it (ויקרא 6:22)
How can both be true? How do they fit together?

steps.whatToRemember: The pot is scoured and rinsed only when the eating time of the קרבן cooked in it is over. This is learned from two פסוקים next to each other.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Abba Yosei ben Abba:
It is written: "And it shall be scoured and rinsed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

phrases.english: and it is written: "Every male among the priests shall eat it."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:22, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: How so?
One waits with it until the time of eating,
and then performs scouring and rinsing on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן אַבָּא: כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about scouring sits next to the פסוק about eating, which teaches that the scouring comes after the eating time.

steps.title: How scouring and rinsing are done: hot or cold water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: scouring is like scouring a cup, and rinsing is like rinsing a cup. A ברייתא then brings an argument: רבי says both are done with cold water, and the חכמים say scouring is with hot water and rinsing with cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: scouring is like the scouring of a cup, and rinsing is like the rinsing of a cup. The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: scouring and rinsing are both done with cold water. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: scouring is done with hot water, and rinsing with cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about how the cleaning is done. It brings a ברייתא where two opinions argue about hot or cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה compares the cleaning to washing a cup, and it says both steps use cold water. The ברייתא shows that this matches רבי's view. The חכמים disagree and say the scouring needs hot water, while the rinsing is done with cold.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the scouring of a cup

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: both scouring and rinsing are done with cold water. חכמים: scouring is with hot water, rinsing with cold.

phrases.english: Scouring is like the scouring of a cup,
rinsing is like the rinsing of a cup.
The Sages taught:
Scouring and rinsing are both with cold water. These are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:
Scouring is with hot water, and rinsing is with cold water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, about how scouring and rinsing are done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי says both scouring and rinsing use cold water. The חכמים say scouring uses hot water and rinsing uses cold water.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים require hot water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the חכמים's view that scouring is done with hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים say scouring needs hot water. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 brought a ברייתא where רבי says both scouring and rinsing use cold water, and the חכמים say scouring uses hot water. Now the גמרא wants to know what the חכמים base their view on.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים from the ברייתא, who said scouring is done with hot water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the חכמים's side of the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the חכמים require hot water for scouring.

steps.title: Like purging vessels bought from non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים compare scouring to גיעולי גוים, purging vessels bought from non-Jews, which is done with hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like the purging of vessels from non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים learn from the case of vessels bought from non-Jews. Those vessels are cleaned with hot water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing what a pot has soaked up needs hot water, as we see with vessels from non-Jews. So the חכמים say the same should be true for cleaning a pot that absorbed קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like, the same as (a comparison)
Purging (with hot water) vessels acquired from non-Jews

phrases.english: It is just like purging the vessels of gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים compare to גיעולי גוים, which use hot water.

steps.title: רבי: hot purging comes first, then cold scouring and rinsing
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that he agrees purging (הגעלה) is done with hot water. His cold-water rule is only about the scouring and rinsing that come after the purging.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי could tell you: I am not talking about purging. I am talking about the scouring and rinsing that come after purging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי would defend himself against the comparison to vessels from non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי splits the process into two stages. First there is a hot-water purging, which he agrees to. Then comes the scouring and rinsing, which he says is with cold water. So the case of vessels from non-Jews does not argue against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Purging a vessel with boiling water

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי holds a pot of קדשים can be cleaned with only cold water. He agrees there is a hot purging first. The argument is only about the scouring and rinsing that follow.

phrases.english: And Rabbi could say to you:
I am not speaking about purging;
when I speak, it is about scouring and rinsing
that come after purging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי's view against the comparison brought in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between stages: hot purging first, cold scouring and rinsing afterward.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to vessels from non-Jews shows scouring must be hot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot water is used for the purging. The scouring and rinsing after it can be cold.

steps.title: The חכמים prove from two different verbs
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue: if scouring and rinsing were the same, the פסוק would use one verb twice. The two different verbs show scouring is hot and rinsing is cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים would say: If so, let the פסוק write either 'scoured, scoured' or 'rinsed, rinsed.' Why does it say 'scoured and rinsed'? Learn from this that scouring is with hot water and rinsing is with cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים bring a proof from the wording of the פסוק that scouring and rinsing must be done in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argue that two different words must mean two different methods. If both were with cold water, one verb repeated would have been enough. So they read it as hot for scouring and cold for rinsing.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say: If so,
let the verse write either 'scoured, scoured'
or 'rinsed, rinsed';
what is meant by 'it shall be scoured and rinsed'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:21

phrases.english: Learn from this: scouring is with hot water,
and rinsing is with cold water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי rejects the comparison, the חכמים bring a proof from the פסוק itself.
steps.raayaObject: That scouring is with hot water and rinsing with cold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק uses two different verbs, 'ומרק ושטף', instead of repeating one.

steps.title: רבי: two verbs mean inside and outside, like washing a cup
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that a repeated verb would have sounded like doing the same act twice. The two verbs teach two different acts, inside and outside like a cup. They say nothing about hot and cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי would say: If it said 'scoured, scoured,' I would think it means scour two times, or rinse two times. That is why it says 'scoured and rinsed,' to tell you that scouring is like scouring a cup and rinsing is like rinsing a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes away the חכמים's proof by giving a different reason why the פסוק uses two verbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees the two verbs mean two different actions. But for him the difference is in what is washed, inside versus outside, like a cup. It is not a difference between hot and cold. This brings us back to the cup comparison from the משנה in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why it is written

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree the two verbs mean two different actions. The חכמים say the difference is hot versus cold. רבי says it is inside versus outside, like a cup, and both can be done with cold water after the hot purging.

phrases.english: And Rabbi would say: If it were written 'scoured, scoured',
I would say: scour two times,
or rinse two times;
therefore it is written 'scoured and rinsed',
to tell you: scouring is like scouring a cup,
phrases.notes: Scouring a cup means cleaning its inside. Rinsing a cup, in the next line, means washing its outside.

phrases.english: rinsing is like rinsing a cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חכמים's reading of the two verbs from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the two verbs for hot versus cold.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two verbs are needed so we don't think one act is done twice. They teach two kinds of washing, inside and outside, not two water temperatures.

steps.title: New משנה: cooking holy and less-holy meat in one pot
steps.stepSummary: If stricter and less strict meat are cooked together and the stricter meat gives taste, the less strict meat is eaten under the stricter rules. But the pot does not need scouring and rinsing because of it, and it does not disqualify other meat by touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone cooked holy meat and regular meat in a pot, or very holy meat and lighter-holiness meat, and the stricter meat gives taste, then the lighter meat is eaten like the stricter meat. But the lighter meat does not require scouring and rinsing, and it does not disqualify by touching.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a mix of stricter and less strict meat cooked together in one pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the stricter meat gives taste, the lighter meat takes on the stricter eating rules: who may eat it, when and where. As printed, the משנה then says the pot needs no scouring and rinsing and the meat does not disqualify by touch. This seems inconsistent, and the גמרא will clarify it in steps 19-20.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives taste (enough to be tasted in the mix)

steps.whyThisMatters: Read plainly, the משנה seems to give one mixture the strict eating rules but lenient rules for the pot and for touching. The גמרא will question this (step 19) and reread the משנה as two separate cases (step 20).

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one cooked in it sacrificial meat and non-sacred meat,
phrases.notes: "In it" means in one pot.

phrases.english: or offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity;
if there is enough in them to impart flavor,
the lenient ones are eaten like the stringent ones among them,
and they do not require scouring and rinsing,
and they do not disqualify through contact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of scouring and rinsing ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the stricter meat gives taste, the lighter meat is eaten under the stricter rules. But it does not require scouring and rinsing, and it does not disqualify by touching.

steps.title: Only the Spot That Absorbed Is Forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when a fit wafer or piece of meat touches an unfit one, only the part that soaked up taste is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a wafer touched another wafer, or a piece of meat touched another piece, not all the wafers or pieces become forbidden. Only the spot that absorbed is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It tells us that touching does not forbid the whole item, only the place that absorbed taste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden taste does not spread through the entire wafer or piece. It stays in the area where the two touched and the taste passed over. Everything else stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin wafer, one kind of מנחה (flour offering)
In the place where it absorbed

phrases.english: A wafer that touched a wafer,
phrases.notes: He means a fit wafer touching an unfit, forbidden one.

phrases.english: and a piece touching a piece –
not all the wafers
and not all the pieces are forbidden;
it is forbidden only in the place where it absorbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about absorbed taste in sacrificial food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a fit item touches an unfit one, only the area that absorbed is forbidden, not the whole item.

steps.title: What Is the משנה Saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means, because its line about stricter and less strict meat seems to contradict itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts and asks what the משנה means. This sets up the next step, where it rereads the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said (step 17) that if the stricter meat gives taste, the less strict meat is eaten under strict rules, yet the pot needs no scouring and the meat does not disqualify by touch. That sounds inconsistent: if the taste counts for eating, why not for the pot and for touching? The short question points at this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A question pointing out unclear or self-contradicting wording

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is puzzled by the משנה from step 17, where one case seemed to get both strict and lenient rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the less strict meat is eaten strictly, but the pot needs no scouring and the meat does not disqualify by touch.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stricter taste counts for eating, it should also count for the pot and for touching. Mixing the results seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Two Separate Cases: With Taste and Without Taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה as two cases. If the stricter meat gives taste, all three strict rules apply. If it does not, none of them apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is enough to give taste, the lenient meat is eaten like the strict meat, the pot needs scouring and rinsing, and the meat disqualifies by touch. If there is not enough to give taste, the lenient meat is not eaten like the strict meat, the pot needs no scouring and rinsing, and the meat does not disqualify by touch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the משנה into two cases. Each case gets the same result for all three rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient parts of the משנה do not belong to the same case as the strict part. They belong to a different case, where the stricter meat gave no taste. So 'with taste' means everything is strict, and 'without taste' means everything is lenient, and nothing contradicts.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives taste, enough of the item to be tasted in the mixture
The less strict meat / the stricter meat
Scouring and rinsing a pot that cooked sacrificial meat
They disqualify other food by touching it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the strict rule and the lenient rules as one case. The גמרא's whole answer is that they are two different cases: with taste and without taste.

phrases.english: If there is enough in them to give taste –
then the lenient ones are eaten like the stringent ones,
and they require scouring and rinsing,
phrases.notes: This means the pot they were cooked in.

phrases.english: and they disqualify by touch;
if there is not enough in them to give taste –
the lenient ones are not eaten like the stringent ones,
and they do not require scouring and rinsing,
and they do not disqualify by touch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: splitting it into two separate cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The strict eating rule and the lenient pot and touching rules seemed to belong to one case, which looked inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: With taste, all three rules are strict. Without taste, all three are lenient.

steps.title: Shouldn't the Pot Need Scouring Because of קדשים קלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'no taste' case: even if the pot needs no scouring because of קדשי קדשים, it should need scouring because it cooked קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted the pot does not need scouring because of the קדשי קדשים. But it should need scouring because of the קדשים קלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks part of its own answer. It asks why the pot is free of scouring in the 'no taste' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without taste, the pot does not get the strict status of קדשי קדשים. But the pot still cooked קדשים קלים, which are sacrificial meat too. The גמרא assumes a pot that cooked קדשים קלים needs scouring anyway, so saying 'no scouring' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that, admitting one point before raising a problem
Let it require, it should need

phrases.english: Granted that because of the most sacred offerings they do not require it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the scouring and rinsing of the pot.

phrases.english: because of the offerings of lesser holiness, let them require it!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לָא בָּעוּ, קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים נִיבְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no taste' half of the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that without taste the pot does not need scouring and rinsing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pot cooked קדשים קלים, and that alone should require scouring, even without any taste from the קדשי קדשים.

steps.title: אביי: the pot is free only from the stricter scouring
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'אין טעונין' means the pot does not need scouring on account of the קדשי קדשים. It still needs scouring on account of the קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What does the משנה mean when it says 'they do not require'? They do not require scouring on account of the קדשי קדשים. But on account of the קדשים קלים, they do require it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 21 by limiting what the משנה's words 'do not require' mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the pot also cooked קדשים קלים, which need scouring. אביי says the משנה never claimed the pot is free from all scouring. It is only free from the scouring that would come because of the קדשי קדשים, since that meat gave no taste. The scouring owed because of the קדשים קלים still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not require (here: scouring and rinsing)
Offerings of the most holy level

phrases.english: Abaye said:
What is the 'they do not require' that it says?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה's words: the pot does not need scouring and rinsing.

phrases.english: [They do not require it on account of] the most holy offerings.
But [on account of] the offerings of lesser holiness, they do require it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the pot needs no scouring at all, even though it cooked קדשים קלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pot is free only from the scouring owed because of קדשי קדשים; it still needs scouring because of the קדשים קלים.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds that pots used for קדשים קלים never need scouring and rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whose opinion is this משנה? It is רבי שמעון, who says that קדשים קלים do not require scouring and rinsing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second way to answer the question from Step 21, by saying which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי kept the rule that קדשים קלים need scouring and limited the משנה's words. רבא keeps the משנה's words as they are, meaning no scouring at all. He explains it by saying the משנה follows רבי שמעון, for whom קדשים קלים never need scouring.

keyTerms.meaning: Scouring and rinsing of the cooking pot

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Shimon,
who says:

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵין טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה.
phrases.english: Offerings of lesser holiness do not require scouring and rinsing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same challenge that אביי answered in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה holds that קדשים קלים need scouring.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, so a pot of קדשים קלים needs no scouring at all.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need two cases according to אביי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's view explains why the משנה adds the case of קדשי קדשים with קדשים קלים. According to אביי, both cases seem to teach the same thing, so why list two?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבא; that is why the משנה teaches: 'or קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.' But for אביי, why do I need two cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer by showing that it makes one of the משנה's cases look unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the second case teaches something new: the pot needs no scouring even for קדשים קלים, like רבי שמעון. For אביי, the pot does need scouring, so the second case only teaches that the taste is cancelled. The first case, holy meat with חולין, already teaches that, so why repeat it?

phrases.english: It works well according to Rava,
this is why it teaches:
'or the most holy offerings and offerings of lesser holiness.'
But according to Abaye,
why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers and challenges אביי's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to אביי, the second case teaches only ביטול, which the first case already taught, so it looks like extra wording.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: first direction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both cases are needed. If only holy meat with חולין were taught, we might think only a different kind of meat can cancel holy meat, not another kind of holy meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it taught only holy meat and ordinary meat, I would say it is ordinary meat that cancels holy meat, because it is not the same kind. But קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by showing the first case alone would leave a wrong idea, so the second case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the first case, we might think ביטול works because חולין is a different kind from holy meat. Then we could think קדשים קלים, being the same kind (holy), cannot cancel קדשי קדשים. The second case teaches that it can.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
They cancel (the forbidden taste or status)

phrases.english: They are needed;
for if it taught [only] holy meat and ordinary meat,
I would have said:
it is ordinary meat that cancels holy meat,
since it is not their kind;
but the most holy offerings and offerings of lesser holiness –
I would say no.
phrases.notes: Meaning: I would think the קדשים קלים cannot cancel the קדשי קדשים, since both are holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24 with a צריכותא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the first case alone, we would think only a different kind of meat can cancel holy meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second case shows that even holy meat of a lesser level cancels holy meat of a higher level.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: second direction
steps.stepSummary: If only קדשי קדשים with קדשים קלים were taught, we might think only holy meat is strong enough to cancel holy meat, not חולין. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it taught only קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים, I would say it is holy meat that is strong enough to cancel holy meat, but ordinary meat, I would say no. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by showing that the second case alone would also leave a wrong idea, so the משנה needs both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the second case, we might think ביטול works because קדשים קלים is itself holy and strong. Then we could think plain חולין is too weak to cancel holy meat. The first case teaches that it can, so neither case is extra.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the pot still needs scouring because of the קדשים קלים. The משנה's two cases both teach ביטול: one shows a weaker, different kind (חולין) can cancel holy meat, and the other shows a same-kind, lower holiness (קדשים קלים) can cancel קדשי קדשים.
steps.confusionAlert: The two reasons point in opposite directions: in one case we worry the meat is too similar to cancel, and in the other we worry it is too weak. That is exactly why each case is needed.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תְּנָא קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
phrases.english: And if it taught [only] the most holy offerings and offerings of lesser holiness,
I would have said:
it is holy meat that is strong enough to cancel holy meat,
but ordinary meat – I would say no;
[so] it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תְּנָא קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in Step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the second case alone, we would think only holy meat is strong enough to cancel holy meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first case shows that even plain חולין cancels holy meat, so both cases are needed and אביי's view stands.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a wafer that touched another wafer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of a רקיק that touched another רקיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A wafer that touched a wafer,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving to a new line of the משנה and quoting its first words as a heading. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה teaches that when a kosher wafer or piece of קדשים touches an unfit one, not everything becomes forbidden. Only the spot that absorbed from the unfit item is affected. The גמרא will now show where this idea of absorbing comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin flat wafer, used in some מנחה offerings
And so on: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: A wafer that touched a wafer, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: only the part that absorbed is forbidden, not the whole wafer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of scouring pots and opens the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a kosher wafer or piece of meat touches an unfit one, only the place that absorbed from it is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא asks whether simple touching is enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes 'כל אשר יגע' and suggests that maybe any touch makes the other item holy, even without absorbing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Whatever shall touch.' You might think this applies even if the other item did not absorb anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that raises a possible first understanding (a הוה אמינא) of the פסוק. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read by themselves, the words 'כל אשר יגע' sound as if any contact at all with the meat of a חטאת passes on its holiness. The ברייתא raises this reading so it can push it away. This is how the ברייתא will tie the משנה's 'absorbing' rule to the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think: introduces a first guess that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'יכול' does not state the law. It offers a possible reading that the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Whatever shall touch"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20, said about the meat of a חטאת.

phrases.english: One might think: even if it did not absorb?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע – יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בָּלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to explain the absorbing rule in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does any touch with the meat of a חטאת make the other item holy, even without absorbing?

steps.title: The word 'בבשרה' shows that simple touching is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק's word 'בבשרה,' which shows that touching alone is not enough. The full explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'with its flesh' (or 'in its flesh').
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by pointing to the word 'בבשרה.' The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בבשרה' can be read as 'in its flesh,' which suggests something going inside the other item, not just touching its surface. This word is how the ברייתא rejects the idea that any touch is enough. It also matches the משנה's rule that only the part that absorbed is affected.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: introduces the proof that answers the 'יכול'
With its flesh, or in its flesh

steps.whyThisMatters: This word is the source in the תורה for the משנה's rule that only the part that absorbed from the other item is affected.

phrases.english: The verse states: "With its flesh"
phrases.notes: בבשרה can also be read 'in its flesh.' The ברייתא finishes the thought right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'יכול' question raised in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בבשרה' (in its flesh) shows that simple touching is not enough. The rest of the answer continues on the next עמוד.
